cells.reason: The California SWRCB hexavalent-chromium MCL of 0.010 mg/L = 10 ug/L (CCR Title 22 section 64431, effective 2024-10-01) is in force, but its product_scope is 'drinking water' delivered by public water systems and its basis is drinking water, not the as-placed-on-market food-content basis of this cooking-oil cell; the regulation page itself states that it does not set a food contaminant level and should not be compared directly to a food concentration, so condition (b) fails. No sovereign food-content Cr-VI limit exists anywhere in the register (every other Cr-VI row is drinking water, toy migration, textile, leather, RoHS, tattoo ink or fertiliser) and GB 2762-2025 expressly sets total chromium only, so there is no same-basis candidate and 10 reproduces only at face value. The nearest same-basis treatment is to bound the species by its parent total (Cr-VI at or below the cell's Cr-total read-across of 300 ug/kg, kind subsumed) or to disclose a baseline screen, not a water MCL presented as a product limit.
